<div class="metronome-launch-box">
  <h3 style="color: #4f6b86; margin-bottom: 15px;">Interactive Metronome Manual</h3>
  <p style="margin-bottom: 20px; color: #666;">Click the button below to open the interactive metronome guide in a new window:</p>
  <a href="/assets/html/Metronome-Manual.htm"

  </a>
</div>

<div class="dropdown-menu">
  <div class="dropdown-item top-level" id="reflection-section">
    <div class="dropdown-question">Reflection</div>
    <div class="reflection-submenus">
      
      <div class="dropdown-item nested">
        <div class="dropdown-question">Initial Thoughts</div>
        <div class="dropdown-answer">
          <p>For my Playing with Design project, I decided to choose a metronome as my object and to build an interactive how to guide using Twine. I had never used Twine before, but I chose it because it seemed both technical and creative as it allowed me to make use of my existing knowledge of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a new way. I built this with introductory musicians and music-lovers in mind as my users.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="dropdown-item nested">
        <div class="dropdown-question">Affordances and Constraints of Twine</div>
        <div class="dropdown-answer">
          <p>As a digital tool, Twine mixes storytelling and interactivity through a "choose-your-own-adventure" style interface. The multimodality of Twine allowed me to create an adjustable metronome with visual feedback and three functioning instruments (snare drum, cowbell, and triangle). I initially started with Harlowe but switched to SugarCube as it provided better scripting for audio and interactivity.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="dropdown-item nested">
        <div class="dropdown-question">Combining Tools and Problem Solving</div>
        <div class="dropdown-answer">
          <p>I combined several technologies including sound files from Universal Soundbank and animations from CodePen. One major challenge was audio latency. Switching to SugarCube allowed me to use the Web Audio API more effectively to overlap sounds without lag. I eventually decided to make the manual a standalone HTML file because of iframe rendering constraints within the blog layout.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="dropdown-item nested">
        <div class="dropdown-question">Pedagogical Perspectives</div>
        <div class="dropdown-answer">
          <p>From an <strong>instructionist</strong> perspective, Twine provided a structured, step-by-step learning process. From a <strong>constructivist</strong> view, the interactivity encouraged pace-based exploration. Finally, from a <strong>constructionist</strong> angle, it allowed users to create artifactual rhythms, making participation shareable and meaningful.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="dropdown-item nested">
        <div class="dropdown-question">Reflection and Future Improvements</div>
        <div class="dropdown-answer">
          <p>Working with Twine was a good exercise in patience and educational design. Despite the learning curve, I see it as a powerful creative tool for educators. In the future, I'd like to improve responsiveness for mobile devices and add skill-testing minigames.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

  </div>

<script is:inline>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  // Handle Reflection top-level toggle
  const reflectionBtn = document.querySelector('#reflection-section .dropdown-question');
  const reflectionSub = document.querySelector('.reflection-submenus');
  reflectionBtn.addEventListener('click', function() {
    reflectionSub.classList.toggle('active');
  });

  // Handle nested items
  document.querySelectorAll('.dropdown-item.nested .dropdown-question').forEach(q => {
    q.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
      this.closest('.dropdown-item').classList.toggle('active');
      e.stopPropagation();
    });
  });

  // Handle References
  const refBtn = document.querySelector('.dropdown-item.top-level:not(#reflection-section) .dropdown-question');
  refBtn.addEventListener('click', function() {
    this.closest('.dropdown-item').classList.toggle('active');
  });
});
</script>

:::note

## Design Note

The metronome manual was developed using the **SugarCube 2.x** story format in Twine to handle simultaneous audio channels across different browser environments.
:::
